Meta spokesperson Francis Brennan stated the company is hiring and training more workers.

title: Travis Kelce expands his business empire with a $53M hydration deal
description: Travis Kelce expanded his growing business portfolio by joining organic hydration company Recover 180 as an investor and brand partner. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end highlighted the importance of quality hydration for peak performance and recovery. The move added to his partnerships across fashion, fitness, food and lifestyle brands. At the same time, Kelce remained focused on football, making it clear that winning another Super Bowl was his biggest goal.

title: Putin orders 3-day pause in strikes on Kyiv as US delegation arrives in Russia
description: US special representatives Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow for crucial peace talks. President Putin ordered a three-day halt to strikes on Kyiv for the American delegation's visit. Both Russia and Ukraine had intensified long-range attacks before this diplomatic engagement. The US push aims to revive efforts to end the ongoing conflict between the nations. The envoys will travel to Ukraine after concluding their discussions in Russia.

title: Kimi Antonelli heads into Monza GP as first Italian championship leader since 1953
description: Andrea Kimi Antonelli enters his home race leading the 2026 Formula 1 championship, becoming the first Italian driver to hold this position before Monza in over seven decades. With an impressive six wins and six pole positions under his belt this season, the stakes heighten as he faces a grid penalty for a power-unit change at the renowned Monza circuit, making this race all the more captivating.

title: From weed smell to a wardrobe fix: Sabalenka, Alcaraz light up unusual US Open day
description: Aryna Sabalenka complained about cannabis smoke during her US Open match.  Kamilla Rakhimova was defeated by Sabalenka in straight sets.  Casper Ruud previously mentioned the pervasive smell of marijuana in New York.  Carlos Alcaraz adjusted his playing attire due to wardrobe concerns.  The Williams sisters experienced a doubles match defeat after a significant lead.

title: Lorry hits BRS president KT Rama Rao’s car in Telangana
description: KT Rama Rao's car experienced a minor collision at Alugunuru junction. A lorry brushed the vehicle's rear door as it was being opened. The BRS leader was inside the car and escaped the incident unhurt. The accident caused slight damage to the car door and brief panic. Rama Rao continued his scheduled program despite the minor mishap.

title: ‘Stop the boats’: Masked men block roads to Dover port in anti-immigration protest
description: Masked men blocked roads leading to Britain's busiest ferry port in Dover. This protest disrupted traffic around the major cross-Channel hub on Saturday morning. Port officials stated that all traffic in and out of the port had been stopped. Videos showed several dozen men dressed in black, shouting "stop the boats". The incident appeared to be an anti-immigration protest, causing significant traffic jams.

title: 7-year-old dies as brick column collapses during Dahi Handi celebrations in Mumbai
description: A seven-year-old boy tragically died during a local Dahi Handi celebration in Malad West.  The accident occurred when a brick column collapsed on the child while playing.  He was rushed to Malvani General Hospital for immediate medical attention.  However, hospital authorities later confirmed the boy was declared brought dead.  The incident took place at Ekta Welfare Society in Chikuwadi, Malvani.

title: DTC fought conductor for 32 years over Rs 67, now fined Rs 1 lakh by Delhi HC
description: The Delhi High Court has imposed a fine of one lakh rupees on the Delhi Transport Corporation for its relentless pursuit of a thirty-two-year-old legal battle involving a bus conductor. The court criticized the drawn-out litigation as an abuse of the legal system. The conductor had been seeking seventeen months of unpaid wages following his dismissal, while the court dismissed DTC's challenge to a tribunal ruling.

title: Where have all the buyers gone? DC homes lose value as demand dries up
description: In Washington, the housing market is revealing an intriguing dynamic, with many properties available at discounted rates—almost one-fifth of homes listed currently are priced lower than what they were purchased for initially. This development points to a slump in buyer interest instead of a surplus of homes for sale. Luxury regions may see upward price trajectories, yet affordable condos are struggling.

title: ‘Always in chaos’: Hayden’s blunt verdict on Pakistan cricket amid latest turmoil
description: Matthew Hayden, the former Australian cricket opener, shared his insights on the persistent instability within Pakistan cricket. He emphasised how this ongoing chaos hampers players' ability to perform consistently. Despite Pakistan's wealth of natural talent, Hayden argued that the country's issues hinder its chances to harness that potential into becoming a cricketing powerhouse on the global stage.

title: NIA court convicts 10 in 2013 Jhiram Valley Maoist attack case
description: A special NIA court convicted all ten accused in the 2013 Jhiram Valley Maoist attack. This attack killed twenty-nine people, including senior Congress leaders, in Bastar district. The court reserved the quantum of punishment for September sixteenth. Statements from one hundred and one witnesses were recorded during the trial proceedings. Defence lawyers plan to appeal the verdict in a higher court.

title: Goa compensates artists with homes destroyed by natural calamities; here's how
description: The Kritadnyata Nidhi scheme in Goa is a boon for artists, providing up to Rs 25,000 for home repairs following disasters. Artists must be Goan citizens, aged fifty or older, with a family income below two lakh rupees to qualify. This welfare initiative extends support to medical needs and various artist services. Notably, age restrictions can be adjusted for those with specific needs or circumstances.

title: Iraq’s petrol problem deepens as OPEC member hit by Hormuz disruption
description: Iraq is grappling with severe petrol shortages as long lines of vehicles form at fuel stations. Ongoing regional conflicts are hindering essential fuel imports, disrupting tanker movement through the vital Strait of Hormuz. The nation heavily relies on these imports to offset domestic production gaps, leading to panic buying and further complicating supply issues. In response, the government is actively seeking additional fuel shipments to replenish reserves.

title: Donald Trump gets mashed over 'small potatoes' Iran war
'Age just a number': Ishan Kishan confident of 'hungry' Shami making India comeback

His exceptional bowling and valuable batting contributions have caught the attention of his captain. The final sees East Zone striving for their first Duleep Trophy title in over a decade, featuring numerous international players and white-ball icons.

With an additional Rs 12.80 crore on Day 2, its total collections in India have surged to Rs 38.55 crore. This theatrical adaptation presents a unique ensemble combining both familiar and fresh faces that engage the audience. Read on to know more.

title: LeT terrorist killed in J&K: Yasir was behind 2024 attack on IAF convoy, civilians
description: Yasir was gunned down on Friday during Operation Ashdar, launched after security forces received intelligence about the movement of a group of terrorists through the Pir Panjal mountains. Jammu and Kashmir Police identified the slain terrorist as Yasir and said he was affiliated with the banned Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT). The police also posted a message on X after the operation, saying, "You Can Run But You Can't Hide!"

title: Five EU countries move towards first ‘return hub’ for rejected asylum seekers
description: Five European Union nations are planning migrant return hubs outside the EU.  These facilities aim to process rejected asylum seekers for repatriation.  The countries hope to finalize agreements with a partner nation this year.  Human rights groups have raised concerns about potential risks to migrants.  The proposed centers are intended to operate within international legal frameworks.

title: ‘Very strange’: Minor’s counsel questions police intent over Bhardwaj’s custody
description: Social media 'influencer' Swatantra Bhardwaj was arrested and sent to one-day police custody. This development followed an alleged assault on a CJP protester's father at Jantar Mantar. Police added provisions of the SC/ST Act and criminal intimidation to the FIR. A fresh FIR was also registered under the POCSO Act for online threats. Bhardwaj's arrest came after CJP representatives demanded action against him.

title: 'Why at 5am?' Owaisi, Akhilesh target UP govt over Saharanpur mosque demolition

description: Uruguay have announced a 46-player preliminary list for upcoming FIFA international matches.  The squad includes prominent players like Federico Valverde and Darwin Núñez.  India will host Uruguay on October 6 in Kolkata.  This match follows India's encounter with Brazil three days prior.  The Panama friendly has been rescheduled to September 25.

title: Sonny Ramadhin: 1st Indian-origin WI cricketer who destroyed England at Lord's in 1950
description: Born in St Charles Village in Trinidad, not far from the capital Port of Spain, Ramadhin lost both his parents when he was a toddler. He was raised by his grandparents, who had migrated from India to work on one of Trinidad's cocoa estates.

title: Sachin honours his 'first teacher' father Ramesh with fellowship for young doctors
description: On Teachers' Day, Sachin Tendulkar paid tribute to his late father, Ramesh Tendulkar, by launching the Professor Ramesh Tendulkar Memorial Fellowship aimed at nurturing young doctors. This fellowship focuses on cleft and craniofacial care specialization, fostering his father's legacy of education as a means of opportunity. Additionally, Tendulkar's foundation promotes initiatives in sports, healthcare, and children's education.

title: Russia hit Ukraine airports ahead of US envoys' visit, Zelenskyy says

Beyond the big four: Why Indian students are preferring Europe?
description: The trend of Indian students pursuing higher education in Continental Europe is on the rise, with Germany taking the forefront, especially in engineering and STEM fields. France and Italy are becoming preferred choices for students interested in business and design. Accessible tuition fees, along with favorable post-study work options, significantly attract these students. Nevertheless, housing and language fluency are crucial factors influencing their success.

title: ‘Babar Azam the next target?’: Ex-Pakistan captain launches scathing attack on PCB
description: The Pakistan Cricket Board is under fire for its management of the national cricket team. Former captain Rashid Latif has accused the board of operating through remote control. The unexpected changes to players and coaching staff mid-series have sparked widespread criticism, further questioning the board's decision-making abilities. As the national Test team battles in the World Test Championship standings, these issues continue to mount.

title: ‘Nothing left for the bowlers’: Suresh Raina sounds alarm over IPL rule
description: Suresh Raina raises alarms about the IPL's impact player rule, arguing it overly benefits batters and inflates scoring. He suggests that Indian players should refrain from engaging in overseas leagues, emphasizing that the Indian Premier League has evolved into a major competition. Furthermore, Raina points out a noticeable decline in the quality of foreign leagues compared to previous years.

title: Canadian billionaire Kevin O’Leary says success requires sacrifice, focus and obsession
description: Kevin O'Leary emphasizes that reaching peak success requires immense dedication and sacrifice. He recommends that individuals focus on three to five key priorities while steering clear of distractions. Influential figures like Mark Cuban and Elon Musk echo similar sentiments, highlighting the role of sacrifice in amassing wealth. O'Leary cautions entrepreneurs to acknowledge failures swiftly, as pouring more resources into failing ideas rarely leads to redemption.

title: ‘CSK captaincy must be changed’: Sanju Samson backed to take over from Ruturaj
description: As Chennai Super Kings prepares for the 2027 season, discussions emerge around the potential of Sanju Samson taking over the captaincy, especially with Ruturaj Gaikwad's performance raising questions. Former cricketer Sadagoppan Ramesh endorses Samson for his invaluable experience and impressive 50% success rate as an IPL captain. CSK must also navigate the future of their coaching staff and the legendary MS Dhoni.

title: 33-year-old buys 81-room Arkansas hotel for $2.55m and spends $1.1m rebuilding
description: From a modest beginning, Greg Clark has embarked on an impressive journey in the hospitality sector, currently breathing new life into an eighty-one-room hotel located in the picturesque Eureka Springs. His aim is to craft exceptional guest experiences, showcasing his renovation progress on TikTok. With a vision to build ten carefully curated hotels over seven years, Clark's journey is one of ambition and creativity.

title: Naomi Osaka vs Serena Williams: How did their 2018 US Open final change her career?
description: Naomi Osaka made history in 2018 by winning her first Grand Slam title against Serena Williams. This pivotal match showcased her exceptional composure, turning what could have been a tumultuous finale into a career-defining moment. Her triumph set the stage for her ascent as a preeminent figure in tennis and a celebrated athlete from Japan, earning her admiration worldwide and paving the way for more significant victories.

title: Jeff Bezos' ex-wife sets new record with donations to historically Black colleges
description: MacKenzie Scott has now donated over one billion dollars to historically Black colleges. Her recent forty-two million dollar gift to Elizabeth City State University marked this milestone. Scott has provided significant funding to numerous institutions since 2020. These unrestricted donations empower universities to allocate funds as needed. Her extensive philanthropic efforts support various educational and community initiatives.
